clue.text: Capital largely welcoming America's right-wing political leader

indicators.note: welcoming means taking in, so the other pieces go inside the trimmed capital
largely means most but not all of the word, so its last letter is dropped

parts.note: Berlin is the capital of Germany
US is short for the United States of America
CON is short for Conservative, a right-wing party

explanation.surface: A capital city mostly welcomes an American right-wing politician.
explanation.walkthrough: 'largely' leaves BERLI, which 'welcoming' opens up; 'Capital' looks like the definition but the politician is.
explanation.definitionFit: Silvio Berlusconi was the long-serving Italian prime minister, a political leader.

clue.text: Tossed picadors (off and on)

indicators.note: tossed means thrown about, so the letters of the next word are rearranged

explanation.surface: Bullfighters on horseback get thrown now and again.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Tossed' rearranges PICADORS.
explanation.definitionFit: Something sporadic happens irregularly, now and then rather than continuously.

clue.text: Country's musical sound

parts.note: Grease is a well-known stage and film musical

explanation.surface: A nation's characteristic music.
explanation.walkthrough: The musical GREASE is said aloud to give the country.
explanation.definitionFit: Greece is a country in south-east Europe.

clue.text: Sardonic about one being lean

indicators.note: about means around, so the first piece wraps the second

parts.note: wry means drily mocking, sardonic
the Roman numeral I is one

explanation.surface: A mocking person comments on someone's thinness.
explanation.walkthrough: 'about' puts I inside WRY.
explanation.definitionFit: A wiry person is lean and sinewy, with no spare flesh.

clue.text: Validity of bequest entailing Cockney injunction to boxer?

a Cockney, dropping his aitches, would urge a boxer to 'hit him' as 'it 'im

explanation.surface: Is a will valid if it involves a Londoner shouting at a fighter?
explanation.walkthrough: Cockney speech, the dialect of East London, drops the H sound, so 'hit him' becomes 'it 'im; 'entailing' is read as containing.
explanation.definitionFit: Legitimacy is the quality of being lawful or valid.

clue.text: Solidly built bunch of idiots?

definitions.meaning: read as two words: a set, or group, of thick, stupid people

explanation.definitionFit: A thickset person has a sturdy, solid build; split in two it is a group of dim people.

clue.text: Press coverage of new and old town

indicators.note: coverage of means covering, so the first piece is wrapped round the second

parts.note: the press is the news media

explanation.surface: Newspapers report on fresh and historic towns.
explanation.walkthrough: 'coverage of' puts N inside MEDIA.
explanation.definitionFit: A medina is the old walled quarter of a North African town.

clue.text: Dynasty with taste

definitions.meaning: the ... ruled China from the 7th to 10th century

explanation.definitionFit: Tang names a Chinese imperial dynasty and also a sharp, distinctive flavour.

clue.text: Fairies engulfing trainee's head in River of Proficiency

indicators.note: in means placed inside, so the fairy piece sits within the river

parts.note: the Exe is a river in Devon, a crossword favourite

indicators.note: a word's head is its first letter

explanation.surface: Sprites surround an apprentice's head in a waterway of skill.
explanation.walkthrough: 'engulfing' builds PERTIS, which 'in' places within the Devon river.
explanation.definitionFit: Expertise is skill or proficiency in a particular field.

clue.text: Laugher longing to interrupt brief laugh

indicators.note: to interrupt means to break into, so one piece goes inside the other

parts.note: ha is a short laugh
a yen is a longing

clue.text: Nearly 100 affected by theft

indicators.note: affected means altered, so the letters are rearranged

parts.note: C is the Roman numeral for 100

explanation.surface: Close to a century of people touched by stealing.
explanation.walkthrough: 'affected' rearranges NEARLY with C.
explanation.definitionFit: Larceny is the legal term for theft of property.

clue.text: Method of divination, taking time, causes irritation

indicators.note: taking means holding inside, so the divination method contains the letter

parts.note: the I Ching is an ancient Chinese book used for divination

explanation.surface: Fortune-telling slowly causes annoyance.
explanation.walkthrough: 'taking' puts T inside ICHING; 'causes' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: Itching is a skin irritation that makes you want to scratch.

clue.text: South Bank plant

parts.note: an edge is a bank or border

explanation.surface: A plant grows on London's South Bank.
explanation.walkthrough: London's South Bank is the arts district on the Thames; here it is split into S and EDGE.
explanation.definitionFit: Sedge is a grass-like plant of wet ground.

clue.text: Mariner's expletive about faulty maps

indicators.note: about means surrounding, so the swear word goes round the other piece

indicators.note: faulty means flawed, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.walkthrough: 'faulty' gives PSMA, which 'about' sets in the middle of a crude British curse.
explanation.definitionFit: A shipmate is a fellow sailor on the same vessel.

clue.text: Goes on spree, perhaps, drunk and over-exposed

explanation.definitionFit: Shop-soiled goods are faded or worn from being on display too long, hence over-exposed.

clue.text: Nearly meet mixture of ingredients

indicators.note: a mixture is a blend, so the letters are mixed up

explanation.surface: A cook almost meets a blend of components.
explanation.walkthrough: 'mixture' rearranges NEARLY MEET.
explanation.definitionFit: Elementary means relating to elements, the basic components of anything.

clue.text: Piece of furniture and ring Caliban locates in "Tempest"?

parts.note: a ring is O-shaped

indicators.note: in a tempest things are blown about, so these letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A ring that Shakespeare's Caliban finds in The Tempest.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in Tempest' rearranges CALIBAN LOCATES. Caliban is the monster in Shakespeare's play The Tempest.
explanation.definitionFit: An occasional table is a small table moved about for occasional use.

clue.text: Minimise importance of function involving food shop

indicators.note: involving means enclosing, so the function wraps the shop

parts.note: sine is a trigonometric function
a deli is a delicatessen, a food shop

explanation.surface: A deli's role belittled.
explanation.walkthrough: 'involving' wraps the trigonometric function round the shop.
explanation.definitionFit: To sideline someone is to push them aside and reduce their importance.

clue.text: Primate's hard at work apprehending hard black sailor

explanation.walkthrough: 'apprehending' wraps the busy word round three short pieces; the 's of Primate's is a link meaning is.

clue.text: Shed's pen quashes fashion for ostentation

mode means fashion

clue.text: Guys accepting help from girl

indicators.note: accepting means taking in, so the guys contain the help

parts.note: guys are men
aid means help

explanation.surface: Men accept assistance from a young woman.
explanation.definitionFit: A maiden is a girl or unmarried young woman.

clue.text: Middle (reportedly) of desert

indicators.note: reportedly means as said aloud, signalling a homophone

parts.note: the waist is the middle of the body

explanation.surface: The centre of a desert, as told.
explanation.walkthrough: The waist, the body's middle, said aloud gives the word for desert.
explanation.definitionFit: A waste is a barren, empty desert region.

clue.text: Ingeniously procure source of wet fish

indicators.note: the source of a word is its first letter

parts.note: to angle is to fish with rod and line

explanation.walkthrough: 'source of' takes W from wet.

A means one
A1 means first-rate, written as AI

clue.text: Tease little boy

definitions.meaning: a shortened form of the boy's name Joshua

explanation.definitionFit: Josh means banter or kid, and is also a pet form of Joshua.

clue.text: Symbol of racket at opening of golf club

parts.note: din means racket, noise

indicators.note: the opening of a word is its first letter

parts.note: a bat is a club

explanation.surface: An emblem of noise at the start of a golf club.
explanation.walkthrough: 'opening of' gives G from golf.

clue.text: Join cut

definitions.meaning: to link up, as spacecraft do
to cut short, as pay or a tail

explanation.definitionFit: Dock means both to couple vehicles together and to reduce or clip.

clue.text: Lustre of the man in the money

indicators.note: in means placed inside, so the man goes into the money

parts.note: sen is a small unit of currency in Japan and elsewhere
he refers to a man

explanation.surface: The gleam of a rich man.

explanation.surface: A blade of past excellence announced.
explanation.walkthrough: EX plus CALIBRE, said aloud, gives the sword.
explanation.definitionFit: Excalibur is King Arthur's legendary sword.
